newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New Bosnia force may help arrest war criminals.
newsitem.headline: New Bosnia force may help arrest war criminals.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher left the door open on Tuesday for a new NATO-led peacekeeping force for Bosnia to take on extra responsibilities for bringing indicted war criminals to justice.
Christopher told a news conference after alliance foreign ministers approved the force that its mandate would be unchanged from that of its predecessor, but additional tasks were not excluded.

"The force will have the same mandate as the prior force did. The capacity that it has to take on additional tasks will depend as it did in the past on whether it has time in addition to its central core of duties to undertake additional tasks."
"It will depend on events in Bosnia if the NATO force is able to move beyond its prescribed tasks," he said.

"The NATO commanders will have the authorisation to assist in additional tasks of the kind you've mentioned but it will depend upon events," he said in reply to a question about whether the force would be able to apprehend suspects and help refugees.
NATO foreign ministers, striving to achieve stability in Bosnia, formally approved a plan on Tuesday to send between 25,000 and 30,000 troops to monitor the Balkan state's peace accords next year.
The 16 ministers agreed that a peace stabilisation force (SFOR) should replace the current alliance-led implementation force (IFOR) when its mandate expires on December 20.
Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy, opening the meeting, said "The continued freedom of indicted war criminals is one of the greatest threats to a durable peace."
"If SFOR departs without having contributed to the apprehension of these people I believe we will have left the seeds of future conflict in Bosnia to germinate."
IFOR, under instructions to detain only suspects who fall into its hands, has not carried out any arrests.

According to a NATO official, one of the strategies he put forward was of "suffocation" whereby indicted criminals would see their freedom of movement restricted and face harassment in a bid to smoke them out.

Christopher said the main thrust of ministers' approach towards detaining suspects was to pressure the Bosnian factions themselves to hand them over and to give more resources to the Hague-based war crimes tribunal.
